scenes.heading: ELT
scenes.narration: ELT is a modern integration pattern where data is extracted and loaded into the warehouse first, then transformed using the warehouse's own compute.

scenes.heading: Why ELT rose to prominence
bullets: Loads raw data quickly, transforms later
Uses the warehouse's powerful, elastic compute
Keeps raw data available for re-transformation
Fits the cloud data stack naturally
scenes.narration: ELT loads raw data quickly and defers transformation to a later step. It leans on the warehouse's powerful, elastic compute to do that transformation in place. Because the raw data stays available, teams can re-transform it whenever requirements change. This pattern fits the cloud data stack naturally, which is why it has become so popular.

scenes.heading: The ELT pipeline
scenes.narration: The ELT pipeline extracts data from its sources first. It then loads that raw data straight into the warehouse. Finally it transforms the data in place using the warehouse's own compute engine.

scenes.heading: ELT vs ETL
scenes.narration: ELT loads raw data first and transforms it inside the warehouse using elastic cloud compute. ETL instead transforms data in a separate layer before loading only the clean result. ELT's flexibility and use of powerful cloud warehouses have made it the dominant modern pattern.

scenes.text: ELT loads raw data first and transforms it in the warehouse, fitting the elastic cloud stack perfectly.
scenes.narration: The takeaway is that ELT loads raw data first and transforms it inside the warehouse, a pattern perfectly suited to the elastic cloud stack.
